title: Prefix Query Suggestions
real_world_story: When a search engine user types a partial query into the search bar, the autocomplete frontend triggers a prefix query to suggest completions. The suggestions must include all dictionary terms sharing that prefix, presented in alphabetical order for predictable user scanning.
problem_statement: Given a dictionary of N search queries and a prefix string P, find all unique queries in the dictionary that start with P. Output the matching queries in ascending alphabetical (lexicographical) order separated by a single space. If no query starts with P, print NONE.
task: Retrieve all words from the dictionary that begin with prefix P and output them in alphabetical order, or NONE.
input_format:
The first line contains an integer N, the number of indexed queries.
The next N lines each contain a lowercase string representing a dictionary query.
The final line contains a string P, the search prefix.
output_format: Print the matching queries sorted in ascending alphabetical order separated by a single space. If no words match, print NONE.

examples.input:
5
apple
application
apply
banana
band
app
examples.explanation: The queries starting with 'app' are 'apple', 'application', and 'apply'. They are printed in alphabetical order.
No query starts with 'dev', so print NONE.

complexity.time: O(|P| + K log K) where K is number of matched words

real_world_takeaway: Locating the prefix node in a Trie allows instant subtree collection of candidate terms, powering interactive autocomplete suggestions.
